title: Celestia Pharma k8s on‑prem hotlist
content:
Topline: capture & prioritize requirements from initial onboarding call with Celestia Pharma (Feb 10) and follow-up technical deep dive (Feb 25). Customer very focused on regulatory auditability (21 CFR Part 11), strict network segmentation, and bringing inference into an existing k8s stack (EKS‑D currently, considering air‑gapped on prem).

Participants (internal): Aisha (SE lead), Marco (infra), Priya (security/compliance), Derrick (syseng).
Participants (customer): Dr. Lena Hsu (ML Lead), Mark Rapp (Platform Eng), Nora Kim (GxP Compliance), Ravi Patel (SRE).

Meeting notes / raw captures:
- Celestia runs a mixed cluster footprint: edge lab clusters (on intel nodes) + central training/infra cluster with A100 instances in their datacenter. They want Redwood Private to serve models close to clinical apps (low latency) and keep PHI inside their network.
- Primary constraint: all inference requests must traverse a validated ingress proxy and be logged to their SIEM (Splunk). No direct outbound to public internet from inference nodes.
- KMS requirement: they use HashiCorp Vault (HSM-backed) for key material. Customer wants Redwood to integrate with Vault and optionally use their HSM for model encryption at rest.
- Audit requirements: immutable logs for model versions, rollout events, and prompt inputs for a 7‑year retention window. Nora flagged 21 CFR/ALCOA+ expectations — need tamper-evident chain.
- Network: strict egress allowlist policy; only specific internal NTP/DNS and Splunk ingest endpoints allowed. NAT gateway not acceptable for inference plane.
- Desire: single operator experience in their k8s (they prefer operator helm chart to manage pods/CRDs). They have GitOps (ArgoCD).
- Runtime: they plan to use dedicated GPUs for production serving; testing on CPU nodes is ok for dev. They request support for FP16 and int8 quantized model variants.
- Scaling: predictable burst model during clinic hours (9am–3pm) with mostly idle overnight. Autoscaling policy must be predictable and within reserved capacity; cannot spin up cloud instances.

Open / clarifying questions I noted (to follow up):
1) Log routing: Do they require Redwood to push telemetry to Splunk or can we ship logs to their S3 bucket and they ingest? Nora preferred Splunk ingest but wants details on format + signed tamper-evidence. (ACTION: Marco to prototype Splunk HEC output; add HEC token lifecycle docs).
2) Vault integration: Are they willing to create a dedicated Vault role for Redwood with limited privileges? Need exact scope. (ACTION: Priya to draft least-privilege role suggestion).
3) HSM usage for model keys: We must verify our runtime supports customer HSM for model key unwrap. Which HSM vendor? (Ravi said Thales + AWS CloudHSM in some regions — ambiguous).
4) ArgoCD operator lifecycle: they want configuration such that upgrades are non-disruptive for active sessions. Can we point them at canary rollout pattern? (ACTION: Derrick to document canary operator pattern and fallback).

Technical gotchas / warnings (from internal):
- Onprem GPU drivers: customers often have mixed driver versions across nodes. Redwood runtime expects NVIDIA drivers >= 525 for Ampere optimizations; if older, we fall back to slower kernels. Need driver check script preflight.
- Kernel / libc mismatches in older distro images cause segfaults for some fused kernels. Recommend standard base image (centos8/ubuntu20 LTS) — confirm with customer.
- Time sync: For signed audit events, clock drift >5s will break signatures. Must ensure NTP is reachable or run Chrony with local stratum.
- Network egress: streaming telemetry plus model downloads may require intermittent egress during updates; for air‑gapped want a manual offline bundle flow (we have an existing offline bundle process but need to test with Celestia's registry).
- Storage: KV cache persists between restarts for latency reasons; if they have ephemeral nodes, we must ensure persistent PVC backed by their SAN/Ceph.

Minimum acceptance criteria (customer):
- Model serving entirely within their network (no model or prompt tokens leave facility).
- Integration with Vault for secrets and KMS for key unwrap tested.
- Audit logs pushed to Splunk HEC with schema agreed (+ test events).
- Canary rollout that guarantees session-affinity during rollout and automatic fallback to previous model on error.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Marco: build Splunk HEC prototype and sample events + ingestion playbook (ETA 2025-03-07) => create JIRA-CEL-1345.
- Priya: Vault least-privilege role draft + step-by-step onboarding doc (ETA 2025-03-05) => attach to JIRA-CEL-1346.
- Derrick: operator upgrade + canary pattern doc, include ArgoCD config snippets and CRD examples (ETA 2025-03-09).
- Aisha: run driver preflight script with Celestia next checkpoint call (schedule week of Mar 10).
- Marco/Derrick: smoke test offline bundle flow with their air‑gapped registry (need registry creds in secure channel).

Notes to self / friction points to track:
- Keep Nora in the loop for every logging spec iteration; she will require sign-off for ALCOA mapping.
- Pricing: customer asked informally if reserved Dedicated capacity can be via monthly on‑prem license. Need to route to commercial ops. (Ping: Kim B. in sales).
- Session persistence semantics: confirm expected maximum KV cache size per model; affects PVC sizing — ask ML team for sample distribution.

Meeting follow-ups / calendar:
- Schedule 1.5h technical runbook workshop with Celestia SRE + our infra owners (target Mar 12).
- Arrange security review with Nora + Priya to walk through audit chain (target Mar 18).

Quick reference commands / links to use in next call:
- preflight: curl -sSL https://internal.redwood.tools/preflight.sh | bash (demo only; customise for client registry)
- offline bundle: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-helm#offline-bundle
- Splunk HEC schema draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/LOGS/Splunk+HEC+schema

Random notes / scratch thoughts (do not send to customer):
- Could offer a signed receipt mechanism (lightweight chain-of-trust) for audit events using customer HSM to sign rollouts — high value for regulated customers. Worth prototyping as optional feature.
- Consider a small on-site proof (2 days) to validate driver/kernel matrix — we might bill as professional services.

End of hotlist. Keep this doc as the running source for boiling down into neat handoffs (Jira tickets + onboarding playbook).

Unresolved: vendor HSM details, exact Splunk ingest rate quotas, and whether Celestia's security policy will permit a short-lived egress for runtime updates (preferred).

Next internal sync: Mon Mar 3, 10:30am PT (prep: Marco to demo Splunk event sample).
